title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 — AI management system
description: A gap-analysis starting point for an AI management system under ISO/IEC 42001:2023. Every requirement in clauses 4 to 10 and all 38 Annex A controls (implementation guidance: Annex B) are defences set to todo. Pair it with the ISO/IEC 27001 template for the security of the AI systems and the EU AI Act template for the law. Titles follow the standard; descriptions are summaries, not the normative text.

risks.title: Harm to individuals or groups from AI system outcomes
risks.description: Outputs or decisions of an AI system treat people unfairly, unsafely or against their rights — discrimination, wrongful denial of a service, physical or psychological harm — and the organization is responsible for it.

risks.title: Compromise or misuse of data used by AI systems
risks.description: Training, validation, input or output data is of unknown origin, unlawfully obtained, poisoned, or exposed through the model itself.

risks.title: AI system does not perform as intended
risks.description: The system is less accurate, robust or available in production than it was when approved, and nobody notices until it has caused damage.

risks.title: AI use cannot be governed or evidenced
risks.description: Nobody owns AI decisions, impacts are not assessed, and there is no record of how systems were built or why — so the organization cannot answer a regulator, a customer or its own board, and loses or never gains certification.

attacks.title: Unrepresentative data or design produces unfair outcomes
attacks.description: Training data under-represents some groups or encodes historical bias, or the objective rewards the wrong thing, and the system reproduces it at scale.

attacks.title: AI system used outside its intended purpose
attacks.description: The system is applied to people, contexts or decisions it was never designed or validated for, by the organization or by its customers.

attacks.title: Consequential decisions issued without meaningful human review
attacks.description: Outputs are acted on automatically, or reviewed by people who lack the time, competence or authority to overrule them.

attacks.title: Performance degrades or drifts undetected in production
attacks.description: The world changes, inputs shift, or dependencies are updated, and accuracy or behaviour moves away from what was validated without anyone monitoring it.

attacks.title: Adversarial manipulation of the model
attacks.description: Prompt injection, evasion inputs or poisoned training data make the system behave as an attacker wants rather than as designed.

references.title: MITRE ATLAS AML.T0051 — LLM Prompt Injection
MITRE ATLAS AML.T0020 — Poison Training Data

attacks.title: Data of unknown origin, quality or lawfulness
attacks.description: Data is acquired or scraped without knowing where it came from, what rights attach to it, or whether it is fit for the purpose.

attacks.title: Personal or confidential data exposed through the AI system
attacks.description: Model inversion, memorisation, verbose logging or careless data preparation reveals the personal or confidential data the system was built or run on.

references.title: MITRE ATLAS AML.T0024 — Exfiltration via AI Inference API

attacks.title: People are not informed about the AI system or its limits
attacks.description: Users and affected people do not know that AI is involved, what it is for, how reliable it is, or how to question an outcome.

attacks.title: Third-party model, data or tooling introduces unassessed risk
attacks.description: A supplier's model, dataset, platform or service is adopted without the organization knowing its behaviour, limits or the responsibilities it has taken on.

attacks.title: AI incident not detected, communicated or corrected
attacks.description: A harmful output or failure happens and is not logged, escalated, reported to the people who must know, or fixed at the root.

attacks.title: AI managed ad hoc: no policy, roles, assessment or review
attacks.description: There is no AI policy, no clear ownership, no repeatable risk and impact assessment, and no review cycle, so decisions about AI depend on whoever happens to be involved.

defences.title: Clause 4.1 — Understanding the organization and its context
defences.description: Determine the internal and external issues relevant to the AI management system, including the organization's roles as AI provider, producer, customer or user, and climate-related issues.

defences.title: Clause 4.2 — Needs and expectations of interested parties
defences.description: Identify interested parties — including those affected by AI systems — and which of their requirements the AI management system will address.

defences.title: Clause 4.3 — Scope of the AI management system
defences.description: Define and document the boundaries and applicability of the AI management system.

defences.title: Clause 4.4 — AI management system
defences.description: Establish, implement, maintain and continually improve the AI management system and its processes.

defences.title: Clause 5.1 — Leadership and commitment
defences.description: Top management owns the AI management system, integrates it into business processes, and provides the resources it needs.

defences.title: Clause 5.2 — AI policy
defences.description: A top-level AI policy, appropriate to the organization's purpose, sets a framework for AI objectives and commits to meeting requirements and continual improvement.

defences.title: Clause 5.3 — Roles, responsibilities and authorities
defences.description: Assign and communicate who is responsible for the AI management system conforming to the standard and for reporting on its performance.

defences.title: Clause 6.1.1 — Actions to address risks and opportunities
defences.description: Plan how to address the risks and opportunities to the AI management system, distinguishing acceptable from non-acceptable risk.

defences.title: Clause 6.1.2 — AI risk assessment
defences.description: Define and apply an AI risk assessment process that identifies, analyses and evaluates risks against the organization's AI objectives and risk criteria.

defences.title: Clause 6.1.3 — AI risk treatment and Statement of Applicability
defences.description: Select treatment options, determine the controls needed, compare them with Annex A, produce a Statement of Applicability justifying inclusions and exclusions, and obtain approval of residual risk.

defences.title: Clause 6.1.4 — AI system impact assessment
defences.description: Define a process to assess the potential consequences of AI systems for individuals, groups and societies across their life cycle.

defences.title: Clause 6.2 — AI objectives and planning to achieve them
defences.description: Set measurable AI objectives and plan what will be done, with what resources, by whom and by when.

defences.title: Clause 6.3 — Planning of changes
defences.description: Carry out changes to the AI management system in a planned manner.

defences.title: Clause 7.1 — Resources
defences.description: Provide the resources needed to establish, run and improve the AI management system.

defences.title: Clause 7.2 — Competence
defences.description: Ensure people whose work affects AI performance are competent — including in the technical and ethical aspects of AI — and keep evidence.

defences.title: Clause 7.3 — Awareness
defences.description: People working under the organization's control know the AI policy, their contribution, and the consequences of not conforming.

defences.title: Clause 7.4 — Communication
defences.description: Decide what is communicated about the AI management system, when, to whom and how.

defences.title: Clause 7.5 — Documented information
defences.description: Create, control and retain the documented information the standard and the AI management system require.

defences.title: Clause 8.1 — Operational planning and control
defences.description: Plan, implement and control the processes that meet AI requirements, including externally provided processes, products and services.

defences.title: Clause 8.2 — AI risk assessment
defences.description: Perform AI risk assessments at planned intervals and when significant changes are proposed or occur.

defences.title: Clause 8.3 — AI risk treatment
defences.description: Implement the AI risk treatment plan and verify its effectiveness.

defences.title: Clause 8.4 — AI system impact assessment
defences.description: Perform AI system impact assessments at planned intervals and when significant changes occur, and keep the results.

defences.title: Clause 9.1 — Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
defences.description: Determine what to monitor and measure about the AI management system, how and when, and evaluate performance and effectiveness.

defences.title: Clause 9.2 — Internal audit
defences.description: Audit the AI management system at planned intervals, objectively, and report the results.

defences.title: Clause 9.3 — Management review
defences.description: Top management reviews the AI management system at planned intervals and decides on improvements and changes.

defences.title: Clause 10.1 — Continual improvement
defences.description: Continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the AI management system.

defences.title: Clause 10.2 — Nonconformity and corrective action
defences.description: React to nonconformities, correct them, remove their causes and keep evidence of the actions taken.

defences.title: A.2.2 AI policy
defences.description: A documented policy for the development or use of AI systems, approved by management.

defences.title: A.2.3 Alignment with other organizational policies
defences.description: The organization determines where other policies — security, privacy, quality, procurement — affect or are affected by its AI objectives.

defences.title: A.2.4 Review of the AI policy
defences.description: The AI policy is reviewed at planned intervals, or when needed, to stay suitable, adequate and effective.

defences.title: A.3.2 AI roles and responsibilities
defences.description: Roles and responsibilities for AI are defined and allocated according to the organization's needs.

defences.title: A.3.3 Reporting of concerns
defences.description: A process lets people in the organization report concerns about its role with respect to an AI system throughout that system's life cycle.

defences.title: A.4.2 Resource documentation
defences.description: The resources each AI system needs — data, tools, compute, people — are identified and documented for every life-cycle stage.

defences.title: A.4.3 Data resources
defences.description: Information about the data resources used for each AI system is documented.

defences.title: A.4.4 Tooling resources
defences.description: Information about the tooling resources — frameworks, libraries, platforms, pre-trained models — used for each AI system is documented.

defences.title: A.4.5 System and computing resources
defences.description: Information about the system and computing resources used for each AI system is documented.

defences.title: A.4.6 Human resources
defences.description: The human resources and competences needed for each AI system's development, deployment, operation, change management, maintenance, transfer and decommissioning are documented.

defences.title: A.5.2 AI system impact assessment process
defences.description: A process to assess the potential consequences of an AI system for individuals, groups and societies throughout its life cycle.

defences.title: A.5.3 Documentation of AI system impact assessments
defences.description: Results of impact assessments are documented and retained for a defined period.

defences.title: A.5.4 Assessing AI system impact on individuals or groups of individuals
defences.description: The potential impacts on individuals or groups — fairness, safety, privacy, access to services — are assessed and documented throughout the life cycle.

defences.title: A.5.5 Assessing societal impacts of AI systems
defences.description: The potential societal impacts — environment, labour, democratic processes, public health — are assessed and documented.

defences.title: A.6.1.2 Objectives for responsible development of AI system
defences.description: Objectives that guide responsible development — fairness, transparency, robustness — are identified and documented, and measures to achieve them are built into development.

defences.title: A.6.1.3 Processes for responsible AI system design and development
defences.description: Specific processes for responsible design and development of AI systems are defined and documented.

defences.title: A.6.2.2 AI system requirements and specification
defences.description: Requirements for new AI systems, or material enhancements to existing ones, are specified and documented.

defences.title: A.6.2.3 Documentation of AI system design and development
defences.description: Design and development are documented according to the organization's objectives, requirements and specification criteria.

defences.title: A.6.2.4 AI system verification and validation
defences.description: Verification and validation measures, with criteria for their use, are defined and documented.

defences.title: A.6.2.5 AI system deployment
defences.description: A deployment plan is documented, and requirements are met before deployment.

defences.title: A.6.2.6 AI system operation and monitoring
defences.description: The elements needed for ongoing operation — system and performance monitoring, repairs, updates and support — are defined and documented.

defences.title: A.6.2.7 AI system technical documentation
defences.description: Technical documentation each category of interested party needs — users, partners, supervisory authorities — is determined and provided in an appropriate form.

defences.title: A.6.2.8 AI system recording of event logs
defences.description: The life-cycle phases in which event logging should be enabled are determined, at minimum while the system is in use.

defences.title: A.7.2 Data for development and enhancement of AI system
defences.description: Data management processes related to developing and enhancing AI systems are defined, documented and implemented.

defences.title: A.7.3 Acquisition of data
defences.description: Details about how data used in AI systems is acquired and selected are determined and documented.

defences.title: A.7.4 Quality of data for AI systems
defences.description: Data quality requirements are defined and data used to develop and operate the AI system meets them.

defences.title: A.7.5 Data provenance
defences.description: A process records the provenance of data used in AI systems over the life cycles of the data and the system.

defences.title: A.7.6 Data preparation
defences.description: Criteria for selecting data preparations — cleaning, labelling, de-identification, transformation — and the methods used are defined and documented.

defences.title: A.8.2 System documentation and information for users
defences.description: The information users need about the AI system — purpose, capabilities, limits, how to use it well — is determined and provided.

defences.title: A.8.3 External reporting
defences.description: Interested parties have a way to report adverse impacts of the AI system.

defences.title: A.8.4 Communication of incidents
defences.description: A plan determines how and to whom incidents involving the AI system are communicated.

defences.title: A.8.5 Information for interested parties
defences.description: The organization determines and documents its obligations to report information about the AI system to interested parties, and meets them.

defences.title: A.9.2 Processes for responsible use of AI systems
defences.description: Processes for the responsible use of AI systems are defined and documented.

defences.title: A.9.3 Objectives for responsible use of AI system
defences.description: Objectives guiding the responsible use of AI systems are identified and documented.

defences.title: A.9.4 Intended use of the AI system
defences.description: The AI system is used according to its intended uses and the accompanying documentation.

defences.title: A.10.2 Allocating responsibilities
defences.description: Responsibilities across the AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.

defences.title: A.10.3 Suppliers
defences.description: A process ensures that services, products or materials from suppliers align with the organization's approach to responsible AI.

defences.title: A.10.4 Customers
defences.description: The organization's approach to responsible development and use of AI considers its customers' expectations and needs.

defences.title: AI liability cover and supplier indemnity (risk sharing under clause 6.1.3)
defences.description: Insurance covering claims arising from AI system outputs, and contractual indemnities from model and data suppliers, as a deliberate decision to share residual risk the controls do not remove.
